split.3a: Landslide susceptibility map v2: trained and validated on NASA landslide reports in ~50 km blocks across south and south-east Brazil, without any Rio Grande do Sul 2024 points; tested on landslides of held-out Brazilian events against random land points.
split.3b: Trigger model: trained and validated on dated NASA landslide reports worldwide, split by event; tested on held-out disaster events never seen in training. NOAA GFS forecasts are scored only on days with an archived forecast run.

t_ml_ranking_note: Susceptibility map, test PR-AUC, calibrated (served scores): best = XGBoost on terrain only 0.765; XGBoost on all inputs (rain, soil moisture, terrain, land cover) 0.747; Random forest (200 trees) on all inputs 0.706; XGBoost on terrain + land cover 0.696. Raw (pre-calibration) scores: best = XGBoost on terrain only 0.765; XGBoost on all inputs (rain, soil moisture, terrain, land cover) 0.747; Random forest (200 trees) on all inputs 0.706; XGBoost on terrain + land cover 0.696. Isotonic calibration (VAL-fit step function) creates ties that lower ranking metrics.

models.xgb_all: XGBoost on all inputs (rain, soil moisture, terrain, land cover)

models.nowcast_xgb_all: XGBoost on rain already observed only (no forecast)

models.direct_rain: One XGBoost per forecast window, on rain only

served.note: The live map uses XGBoost on rain + soil moisture: one daily model, combined over the days of each forecast window. On the validation events, one XGBoost per forecast window (rain only) ranked slightly higher (by at most 0.02 PR-AUC); both are reported on the test events.

val_vs_test_note: Validation = held-out landslide reports worldwide (NASA landslide catalogues, mostly 2015-2018, scored with observed rain). Test = held-out disaster storms. Validation PR-AUC (24 h, about 0.13) is about 5x lower than on the test storms (about 0.62), because the test storms are large and well dated. An independent audit found no leakage: the test events are easier by design, so read the test scores next to the validation scores. A simple rule - rain compared with the local 1-in-100-day level - scores about the same.
headline_status: audited: no leakage; scores overstate everyday skill (extreme-storm test set); similar to a simple rain-threshold rule

audit.verdict: No leakage or overfitting found. The test events are extreme storms, so test scores overstate everyday skill; the ML performs about as well as a rule comparing rain with the local 1-in-100-day level.

by_lead.definition: lead k: forecast issued on D-k (GFS 00Z run of D-k), scored on the shortest horizon whose window reaches the event day D; RS 2024 D = 2024-05-01 (fixed), WA 2025 D = reported date
by_lead.availability_note: k = 0 is the 00Z run of day D: GFS 00Z is available ~3.5-4 h after 00Z, i.e. at or after an onset at local midnight in Brazil, so it is NOT 'before the damage'. Claims of 'before the onset' use k >= 1 (run issued >= 24 h before D), matching lead-analysis warned% (L37).

negatives.same_point: TEST positive points on event-free dates (>=30 d gap), scored with the horizon of k
negatives.elsewhere: TEST elsewhere-same-day points (5-50 km away) issued on D-k

by_lead.thresholds: VAL-fit per-horizon F1 thresholds (calibrated P); rule_tpi 0.6
by_lead.precision_note: case-control negatives: precision/accuracy are not real-world rates
by_lead.served_note: served_product = calibrated P_trigger(xgb_rain_soil) x T_ML (the live layer); ranking metrics only, no threshold was fit for it
by_lead.clean_3a_note: <scope>_clean3a keeps only positives >= 5 km from every 3a TRAIN/VAL/buffer positive: the only scope where served_product (x T_ML) is leak-free
